attempts.summary: Installed a daily 02:15 cron job on node1 that runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance and appends output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Along the way, fixed the pre-existing script file, which contained leftover heredoc/install artifacts instead of a clean executable script (it was not executable and had garbage trailing lines). Rewrote it as a valid #!/bin/sh script, set 0755 root:root ownership/permissions, and verified it runs successfully. Created /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance with the schedule "15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1" and confirmed crond is active/enabled. Manually exercised the exact cron command line to confirm it creates and appends to the log file correctly. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and service/data state, issued a safe `shutdown -r now`, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (fb2aa416... -> 160e0496...) proving an actual restart (not just a service bounce), and verified post-restart that crond is active/enabled, the cron.d file and script are intact, the script still runs successfully, and the log file's pre-reboot entry persisted.
